## Why

I chose a consecrated lily as the single recognizable subject for *Sacra Virginitas* because it is the pre-eminent iconographic symbol of purity, chastity, and consecrated virginity, often associated with the Virgin Mary and saints who embraced celibacy. The inclusion of a delicate, integrated crown emphasizes the positive aspect of consecration—spiritual marriage to Christ as a high calling, rather than just an absence of marriage—fulfilling the central argument of the text. An abstract form was rejected because it could not instantly communicate the concept of sacred purity and spiritual fidelity with the same immediacy and recognized devotion as this concrete symbol.

## Text-to-image prompt

A single, monumental, masterfully sculpted representation of a consecrated lily, sculpted from a single block of flawless, warm white marble with subtle gold veining, standing vertically on a simple, square, fluted plinth of dark, polished basalt. The subject is instantly recognizable as a single lily flower with an upright, graceful stem, six large, elegant petals unfurling in a symmetrical form around a detailed cluster of stamen and pistil. Integrated into the center of the bloom, subtly crowning the internal elements, is a delicate, small crown made of hammered gold with tiny ruby and sapphire inclusions, representing spiritual marriage. The sculpture has refined geometry, realistic micro-surface texture on the marble showing subtle chisel marks and natural stone grain, and a premium finish of a luxury sacred object.

Rendered as a high-end Cinema 4D / Octane physically based 3D render with global illumination, ray-traced reflections, and pronounced ambient occlusion in the floral recesses and plinth grooves. The camera is dead-center, 85mm lens equivalent, at object mid-height, looking straight frontally with symmetrical composition. Dramatic, high-contrast chiaroscuro lighting comes from a strong upper-front-left key light, casting deep shadows on the right while creating luminous highlights on the polished marble petals. A crisp rim light carves the silhouette against a perfectly transparent background (alpha channel), with no environment or floor visible.

## Why

I selected a crowned lily to translate *Sacra Virginitas*, as the lily is the definitive symbol of purity and virginity in Christian iconography. The small gold crown nested within the petals symbolizes "consecration"—the encyclical's positive definition of virginity as a "spiritual marriage to Christ" rather than just an absence of activity. I rejected abstraction because a specific, recognizable, and traditional devotional symbol is required to communicate this particular theological virtue clearly to the viewer without explanation.

## Text-to-image prompt

A cinematic 3D product render in the style of Octane Render, featuring a single, monumental marble sculpture of a crowned lily against a transparent background (alpha channel). The sculpture is carved from a flawless, warm-toned polished marble, depicting a fully bloomed lily flower on a tall, elegant stem rooted in a simple, fluted dark basalt plinth. The carving is highly detailed, showing natural marble grain and precise petal definitions. A delicate, small gold wire crown sits within the center of the bloom, catching the light. The lighting is dramatic high-contrast studio lighting, with a primary key light from the front-left generating strong highlights on the marble and deep shadow falloff on the opposite side, emphasizing the 3D form. There are pronounced ambient occlusion shadows in the petal recesses. The camera is set at eye-level, dead-center, with a neutral 85mm lens perspective and zero tilt, capturing the full object symmetrically. The texture has realistic material response and micro-surface details. There is no text in the image.
